response.title: is an extra battery for a power station worth it or should i buy a second one
response.answer:
In most cases, I'd recommend buying a second power station rather than an expansion battery, especially if the prices and battery capacities are similar.

However, if you're building a home backup system and need longer runtime for high-power appliances, an expansion battery can be the better investment.

Expansion battery vs. second power station

When I'd choose each
Shop

Buy an expansion battery if:

You're mainly using the station for home backup, want longer runtime for a refrigerator or other appliances, and don't need more AC output or charging inputs.

Shop

Buy a second power station if:

You want redundancy, more outlets, independent solar charging, or the ability to use power in two locations. It's also safer against a single inverter failure.

The important factor most people overlook

An expansion battery typically increases energy capacity (Wh), not inverter output (W).

For example, suppose you have a 1,000Wh power station with a 1,500W inverter.

Adding a 1,000Wh expansion battery gives you 2,000Wh total, but still only 1,500W AC output.

Buying another 1,000Wh power station gives you 2,000Wh combined capacity and two independent inverters, although you generally can't combine their outputs to power one large appliance.

Also, two independent power stations can potentially charge from solar simultaneously, making a big difference during extended outages.

My rule of thumb

If an expansion battery costs less than 65–70% of a comparable second power station, I'd seriously consider it.

If the prices are within 20–30%, I'd lean toward the second station for its flexibility and redundancy.

These are rules of thumb, not hard thresholds. Charging speed, inverter quality, compatibility, and warranty also matter.

Which power station do you currently own? (EcoFlow DELTA, Bluetti AC200, Anker SOLIX, Jackery, etc.)

If you tell me the exact model, I can compare the expansion battery against a second station based on actual prices, capacity, and functionality.
